title: 第5章 第一堂课
novel_title: 御兽仙朝：我能设计进化形态
content_zh:
潜鳞书院的大门比牌坊还气派。

    两扇朱漆木门，门板上铆着铜钉，排列得整整齐齐，日头照上去亮闪闪的一片。

    门槛足有一尺高，黑石料打磨的，光溜溜的，被进进出出的脚底板蹭出了一层包浆。

    门楣上方蹲着一只石雕的【鉴血灵蝉】，通体灰白，翅翼收拢，两只圆鼓鼓的眼珠子朝下望着，像是在打量每一个踏进门的人。

    罗影跨过门槛的时候，不由自主地抬头看了那只石蝉一眼。

    蒙学里胡师讲过，潜鳞书院的新生入学仪式上，会有真正的【鉴血灵蝉】落在学生肩头鸣叫，鸣叫的时长代表潜力的高低。

    不过那是后面的事了。

    现在先要交出银子。

    过了大门之后，前面出现了一条青石铺成的通道。

    两边种着大约半人高的灵竹，叶子呈淡青色荧光。

    在风吹过时发出沙沙的声音，比一般的竹子要清脆得多。

    甬道的尽头有一面照壁，照壁之后就是书院的前院。

    前院很大，铺着方砖，四角各立着一根石柱，柱顶上蹲着四只【巡课纸鸢】。

    纸鸢通体灰白，翅膀折叠着，一动不动，像是石雕。

    但罗影注意到，它们的眼珠子在转。

    前院左边有一排厢房，门上挂着木牌，上面写着“缴费处。”

    已经有很长的队伍排好了。

    罗影、李子诚走过来站到最后一个位置上。

    前面的人三三两两地向前移动。

    有的抱着钱匣子...

    有的腰间挂着鼓鼓的荷包...

    还有的穿着和罗影差不多的打扮，背着包袱，缩着肩膀，眼里带着一种藏不住的拘谨。

    队伍走得并不算慢。

    缴费窗口后面坐着一个中年文吏，面前摆着算盘和账簿，身旁蹲着一只【吞钱蟾】。

    蟾蜍肚皮鼓鼓的，嘴巴张着，铜钱银锭丢进去，肚子里就传出“叮”的一声脆响，比算盘拨得还快。

    当轮到罗影的时候，他就把书箱从背上拿下来，打开书箱，取出里面包裹的三层旧布。

    麻绳为死结，他解了两下之后才解开。

    布层一层地揭下来，里面的物品就会暴露出来。

    一双牛角。

    乌黑发亮，弧度非常标准，在断口处有一圈不规则的毛茬。

    放在柜台上面的时候，发出“嘭”的一声。

    中年文吏抬了抬眼皮，在牛角上停顿了一下。

    面无表情地拿起牛角掂了掂，然后用手指在牛角面上弹了一下，又靠近了牛角，仔细观察它的纹路。

    “觉醒二级黑水牛角，实心，灵纹正，品相完美。”

    拿起笔，在账簿上记下一行。

    “折银六两，束脩已缴。”

    把牛角放在柜台后面的一个木匣子里，和其他灵材一起码放在一起。

    就这么几息的功夫。

    老黑在石柱上撞了不知道多少次，才卸下的东西...

    成为了账簿上的一行墨迹。

    罗影看着那只木匣子，没说话，把空了的旧布叠好，塞回书箱里。

    李子诚站在他身后。

    他什么都看见了。

    牛角。

    黑水牛的牛角。

    他认得。

    罗家那头老黑，他见过不止一回，小时候去罗家村串门，还骑过它的背。

    那对角又黑又亮，硬得跟铁似的，是老黑身上最精神的物件。

    可现在，它断了，搁在柜台上，被一个文吏面无表情地丢进了木匣子里。

    李子诚的喉结动了一下。

    他没有问。

    不用问。

    他家住在县城，杂货铺一年的进项十来两，比罗家殷实，但也就殷实那么一点。

    六两束脩他爹攒了大半年，咬着牙才掏出来。

    如果他这半年没过考核，被劝退了，他家还有再来一回的底子吗？

    恐怕也没有。

    他跟罗影之间的距离，没有他以为的那么远。

    只不过罗影家，连这六两都得用一头老牛的角来换。

    李子诚走上前，把自己的银子递了过去。

    六两整，碎银子，拿布包着的。

    文吏收了，算盘拨了几下，账簿上又添了一行。

    两个人一前一后离开缴费窗口。

    走了几步，李子诚忽然注意到旁边经过的一个少年。

    那少年穿着一身月白色的细棉直裰，腰间佩着一枚碧玉环，身后跟着一个仆从，仆从手里捧着一只锦缎盒子。

    盒子打开的时候，罗影也看见了。

    里面整整齐齐地码着银锭。

    不是六两。

    起码十几两。

    文吏收那盒银子的时候，脸上的表情跟收他们那六两时截然不同，多了一丝客气，甚至欠了欠身。
content_en:
The gate of Qianlin Academy is more impressive than the archway.

Two red-lacquered wooden doors, with copper nails riveted on the door panels, were arranged neatly and shone brightly in the sun.

The threshold is a foot high and made of polished black stone. It is smooth and has a layer of patina from the soles of the feet that go in and out.

Above the lintel squatted a stone-carved "Blood-Detecting Cicada". It was all gray and white, its wings were folded, and its two bulging eyes were looking down, as if it was sizing up everyone who stepped through the door.

When Luo Ying crossed the threshold, he couldn't help but look up at the stone cicada.

In Meng Xue, Teacher Hu once said that during the entrance ceremony for new students at Qianlin Academy, a real [Blood Appraisal Cicada] would sit on the students' shoulders and chirp, and the duration of the chirp represented the level of potential.

But that’s later.

Now we have to hand over the money first.

After passing the gate, a passage paved with bluestone appeared in front.

There are spiritual bamboos about half a person's height planted on both sides, with light cyan fluorescent leaves.

It makes a rustling sound when the wind blows, which is much crisper than ordinary bamboo.

There is a screen wall at the end of the corridor, and behind the screen wall is the front yard of the academy.

The front yard is very large, paved with square tiles, with a stone pillar standing at each corner, and four [class patrol kites] squatting on the top of the pillar.

The kite is all gray and white, its wings are folded and motionless, like a stone sculpture.

But Luo Ying noticed that their eyes were moving.

There is a row of side rooms on the left side of the front yard, with a wooden sign hanging on the door that reads "Payment Office."

There is already a long queue.

Luo Ying and Li Zicheng came over and stood in the last position.

The people in front moved forward in twos and threes.

Some are holding money boxes...

Some have bulging purses hanging around their waists...

Others were dressed similarly to Luo Ying, carrying baggage, hunched shoulders, and an unconcealable restraint in their eyes.

The team was not moving too slowly.

There was a middle-aged clerk sitting behind the payment window, with an abacus and account books in front of him, and a [Money Swallowing Toad] squatting next to him.

The toad's belly was bulging and its mouth was open. When the copper coins and silver ingots were thrown in, there was a crisp "ding" sound in the belly, faster than the abacus.

When it was Luo Ying's turn, he took the book box off his back, opened the book box, and took out the three layers of old cloth wrapped inside.

The hemp rope was knotted, and he untied it twice before untying it.

As the layers of cloth are peeled off, the contents will be exposed.

A pair of horns.

Black and shiny, the curvature is very standard, and there is a circle of irregular stubble at the break.

When it was placed on the counter, it made a "bang" sound.

The middle-aged civil servant raised his eyelids and paused on the horns.

He picked up the horn and weighed it expressionlessly, then flicked the surface of the horn with his fingers, then got closer to the horn and carefully observed its lines.

"Awakened level two black buffalo horn, solid, with correct spiritual patterns and perfect appearance."

Pick up a pen and write down a line in the ledger.

"Sixty taels of silver are broken, and the bundle has been paid."

Put the horns in a wooden box behind the counter and stack them with other spiritual materials.

It only takes a few breaths.

Lao Hei bumped against the stone pillar countless times before unloading...

It became a line of ink on the account book.

Luo Ying looked at the wooden box, said nothing, folded the empty old cloth and stuffed it back into the book box.

Li Zicheng stood behind him.

He saw everything.

Horns.

Black buffalo horns.

He recognized it.

He had seen the old black guy from the Luo family more than once. When he was a child, he went to visit Luojia Village and even rode on its back.

The opposite corner was black and shiny, as hard as iron. It was the most energetic thing on Lao Hei's body.

But now, it was broken, lying on the counter, and was thrown into the wooden box by a clerk with an expressionless face.

Li Zicheng's Adam's apple moved.

He didn't ask.

No need to ask.

His family lived in the county seat, and the grocery store's annual income was about ten taels, which was better off than the Luo family, but only a little more prosperous.

His father had been saving six liang bunches for more than half a year, and he gritted his teeth before taking them out.

If he failed the assessment in the past six months and was persuaded to quit, would his family have the foundation to come back again?

Probably not.

The distance between him and Luo Ying was not as far as he thought.

It's just that Luo Ying's family had to exchange these six taels with the horn of an old cow.

Li Zicheng stepped forward and handed over his money.

Six taels, broken silver, wrapped in cloth.

The clerk took it away, dialed the abacus a few times, and added another line to the account book.

The two people left the payment window one after the other.

After walking a few steps, Li Zicheng suddenly noticed a young man passing by.

The young man wore a moon-white fine cotton trousers and a jade ring around his waist. He was followed by a servant, who held a brocade box in his hand.

When the box was opened, Luo Ying also saw it.

Silver ingots were neatly stacked inside.

Not six taels.

At least a dozen taels.

When the clerk received the box of silver, the expression on his face was completely different from when he received the six taels from them. He was a little more polite and even bowed.
